case.question: How long do we have to dispute a missing-item chargeback on an Uber Eats order?

trace.question: How long do we have to dispute a missing-item chargeback on an Uber Eats order?
trace.answer:
You have 30 days from the order date to dispute a missing-item chargeback on an Uber Eats order. A dispute filed after that is rejected automatically [marketplace: Missing or incorrect items].

You also need a packing photo showing the item in the bag. Photos are taken at the pass for every marketplace order over $40. If an order was over $40 and has no photo, don't dispute it. Accept the chargeback and log it as a packing miss.

trace.question: A Grubhub customer complained the food arrived cold. We marked the order ready 15 minutes before it was actually done. Is that on us?
trace.answer:
Yes, on this one it is on you. The marketplace policy normally makes cold or late delivery the platform's cost once the courier has picked up the order. It carves out one exception: a Grubhub order that was marked ready more than 10 minutes before it was actually ready. That counts as your delay, and you accept the chargeback [marketplace: Late, cold, or damaged deliveries].

You marked this order ready 15 minutes early, which is past the 10-minute threshold. So you shouldn't dispute the chargeback, and you shouldn't send the customer to Grubhub support to dodge it. I haven't looked up the specific order, so the 15-minute figure is the one you gave me.

trace.question: An Uber Eats order was cancelled 90 seconds after we confirmed it. Do we still get paid?

trace.question: Can we text our list a 20% off deal?
trace.answer:
Not as written. I proposed the campaign, and the check blocked it. Nothing was sent.

- **Discount cap:** Texted discounts can't go over 15% or $10, whichever is lower, unless the owner approves [messaging: Offers in messages]. 20% is over that cap. The check blocked the proposal for that reason, and it didn't route it to you for approval. If you want to run 20%, you'd need to get owner approval first. Otherwise, a 15% offer would fit the cap.
- **Audience:** Only 108 of your 4,817 customers can get a marketing text. They have verified SMS consent and haven't unsubscribed [messaging: Who may receive marketing texts]. Another 2,848 customers gave a phone number but never opted in. That is implied consent, which isn't enough for marketing texts.
- **Offer wording:** The offer must expire within 14 days and say "one per customer" [messaging: Offers in messages]. My draft expires 2026-11-03 and includes both.
- **Send time:** Texts can't go out between 8pm and 9am in the customer's local time [messaging: Quiet hours].

I can resubmit the campaign at 15% if you'd like.

case.question: How many stamps earn a free drink, and can it be used on a Seasonal Special?

trace.question: How many stamps earn a free drink, and can it be used on a Seasonal Special?
trace.answer:
Nine stamps earn a free drink. It can't be used on a Seasonal Special. The loyalty program excludes Seasonal Specials, Flights, and Bubble Tea from the free drink [online-orders: Loyalty program]. The free drink can be any size from Signature Drinks, House Favorites, or Matcha.

Seasonal Specials are also never discounted [house: Discounts].

You earn one stamp per drink, and the customer has to give a phone number at checkout. Stamps expire 12 months after they are earned. Once a free drink reward is issued, it expires after 60 days [online-orders: Loyalty program].
